 Brazoria County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0047
 Susan Ramirez, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Susan Ramirez
Date:
July 9, 2025
Location:
Offices of Brown & Shaw Law Group
Examining attorney:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Sarah Combs, Brown & Shaw Law Group
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd prefer to keep my name off the record for now, but I can answer the questions.
Q: Let's start with the accident itself. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Baytown, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. It was a weekday afternoon and traffic
was light.
Q: Describe what happened right before the collision.
A: A car came over the center line and was coming straight at me. I braked and turned slightly to the right, but we still hit nearly
head-on. It wasn't a high-speed crash. I'd say we were both going well under the posted limit, but the impact was enough to set off
the airbags.
Q: Did you lose consciousness?
A: I don't tihnk I fully blacked out, but everything went hazy for a few seconds. I remember my head snapping forward and then
hitting the headrest.
Q: What symptoms did you notice in the days after?
A: The headache started within a few hours and didn't go away. I felt foggy, had trouble focusing on conversations, and light
bothered my eyes. I also got dizzy when I stood up too quickly.
Q: Who did you see for treatment?
A: I went to the emergency room the same day. They did a CT scan and told me I had a concussion. After that I saw my primary
care doctor and was referred to a neurologist.
Q: Are you still receiving treatment?
A: Yes. I have follow-up appointments and I do some vision and balance exercises with a therapist twice a week. My doctor told
me the recovery could take a while.
Q: How has this affected your daily life?
A: I had to step back from work for several weeks. Reading for long periods is hard, and I get tired quickly. I used to coach my
kid's soccer team and I had to hand that off to my spouse. I also stopped driving for a while because my reaction time felt off.
Q: Have your symptoms improved since the accident?
A: Some of them have. The headaches are less frequent now, but I still have bad days where the fog comes back, especially when
I'm stressed or tired.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about your injuries?
A: Only that I'm doing what my doctors ask me to do. I want to get back to normal, and I'm working at it every day.
</page>
